newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh faces new influx of Burma refugees.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh faces new influx of Burma refugees.

text.p: Burmese Moslems, complaining of a growing food shortage and continuing persecution by Rangoon's military junta, have started to flee again into Bangladesh, officials said on Monday.
"At least 5,000 Moslems were detected to have crossed into Cox's Bazar district from Burma's western Arakan province over the last two months," one official said.
"But border guards and police could arrest only about 1,500 of them and pushed them back home across the Naf river," he said.
The rest of the Moslems, called Rohingyas, mingled with local people or fled into the nearby hills, he told Reuters.
More than 250,000 Rohingyas fled to southeastern Bangladesh in early 1992 from Arakan, complaining of military persecution and forced labour.
Repatriation, supervised by the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), began in September that year following an agreement between Dhaka and Rangoon.

Others sources said 7,000 or more Rohingyas had sneaked into Bangladesh in the new influx, which began as Bangladesh was awaiting clearance from Burma to repatriate some 21,500 Rohingyas who had been living in Bangladesh refugee camps since 1992.
"New refugees are flowing in despite high alert on the border," one official in Teknaf border town said.
"The infiltrators often mix up with people living along the frontiers," said Colonel Waliullah of the Bangladesh Rifles (BDR), border force.
"We have asked for cooperation (of local residents) to detect and arrest the infiltrators, who might include some armed elements in the guise of refugees," he said.
"People are responding to our plea...and their actions would definitely discourage the illegal migrants," he said without elaborating.
Waliullah said the BDR also asked the Burmese border guards to tighten checks on their side to curb the flow of Rohingyas.
Officials said Bangladesh had rejected a proposal by an international organisation to grant the remaining 1992 refugees Bangladeshi nationality.
"We had the request from an international organisation but it was immediately turned down," said a senior official, who declined to be named.

"This request came in view of the delay by Myanmar (Burma) in taking back their people, but we told them that Bangladesh would never accept Burmese refugees as its citizens," the official told Reuters on Monday.
"Even such hints would encourage new influx. We are already swamped by problems of our own and we cannot afford to invite others."
